gaps.sentence: Her ___ (JUDGE) of character is rarely wrong.
gaps.explanation: 'Her judgement of character' — the noun follows the possessive.

gaps.hint: noun needed after 'signs of'; note the spelling change
gaps.explanation: After 'signs of' a noun is needed: recovery (the -er of 'recover' becomes -ery).

gaps.sentence: There has been a big ___ (IMPROVE) in her tennis.
gaps.explanation: After 'a big' a noun is needed: improvement (-ment noun).

gaps.sentence: The referee sent him off for repeated ___ (OBEY).
gaps.explanation: 'Repeated disobedience' — the negative noun follows the adjective.

gaps.sentence: She is very ___ in modern art (INTEREST).
gaps.hint: how she feels: -ed; fixed pattern '___ in'
gaps.explanation: 'Interested in something' describes the person's feeling; 'interesting' describes the thing that causes it.

gaps.sentence: The trip gave us a lot of ___ (PLEASE).
gaps.explanation: 'A lot of' needs a noun: pleasure (note the irregular spelling).

gaps.sentence: He answered all the questions with great ___ (CONFIDENT).
gaps.explanation: 'Great' needs a noun: confidence. 'Confident' is the adjective.

gaps.sentence: She was praised for her ___ (TOLERATE) of other viewpoints.
